messages:
alex: quick heads-up — ran nvprof + perfetto on the perf-cluster (A100x4) for the batch/kv workload. seeing one kernel spike that wasn't obvious before: kv_cache_evict seems to be ~40-45% of GPU time across traces :eyes:
maria: ugh that's higher than expected. which stage? warmup or steady-state?
alex: steady-state, after warmup. seq=1024, target batch=8. nvprof summary pasted below:
```
== Profiling result ==
Kernel: kv_cache_evict    Calls: 128    Total GPU Time: 42.1%    Avg: 0.78ms
Kernel: attn_fwd          Calls: 1024   Total GPU Time: 18.3%    Avg: 0.14ms
Kernel: softmax_fold      Calls: 512    Total GPU Time: 9.6%     Avg: 0.19ms
Kernel: kv_prefetch       Calls: 256    Total GPU Time: 7.2%     Avg: 0.23ms
```
jon: can you paste the perfetto timeline clip? curious if this is serialized on CPU or pure SM time
alex: uploaded small perfetto slice to the trace bucket, link in thread (perfetto://perf/trace/4150001234) — looks like kv_cache_evict fires serially across batches, long tails on some warps
leena: did we change eviction heuristics recently? I recall a batching tweak last week that touched KV churn thresholds
maria: yeah, the heuristic lowered the prefetch window to reduce memory pressure — maybe aggression caused more evictions. @leena do you have the PR number?
leena: PR #4128 — reduced prefetch_window from 32->16 for low-memory mode. it was to avoid OOM on small nodes
jon: hypothesis: smaller window => more frequent evicts => more frequent kv_cache_evict kernel launches and lower occupancy per launch. can we validate occupancy numbers from nvprof?
alex: pulled occupancy and SM util for the top kernels:
```
kv_cache_evict: active warps/SM 10/64 (low occupancy), achieved_occupancy 0.16, avg SM util 28%
attn_fwd: active warps/SM 40/64, achieved_occupancy 0.62, avg SM util 78%
softmax_fold: active warps/SM 18/64, achieved_occupancy 0.28, avg SM util 45%
```
maria: that occupancy for kv_cache_evict is bad. low active warps means kernel launch overheads dominate.
leena: could be also poor block sizing after the prefetch change. are we launching tiny grids for small per-sample work?
alex: yes. grid sizes vary per batch item because the eviction set is dynamic. with smaller prefetch_window most items have tiny eviction sets => many tiny kernel launches.
jon: two mitigation paths: 1) coalesce evictions into a single batched kernel per-device tick (amortize launch cost) 2) change heuristic to avoid tiny eviction-set launches (threshold merge)
maria: option 1 looks promising but needs to ensure correctness (ordering of K/V evicts vs subsequent loads). option 2 is faster to roll back (bump prefetch_window)
ale x: quick microexperiment: merged evictions per-batch on a dev node (single kernel handles all items) — nvprof after change:
```
kv_cache_evict_coalesced: Calls: 8    Total GPU Time: 18.4%    Avg: 2.4ms    achieved_occupancy 0.58    avg SM util 72%
attn_fwd: unchanged
```
leena: that's a 2x drop in overall kv kernel time, nice. any tail effects?
alex: tails reduced, perfetto slice shows fewer serialized launches and better overlap with attn_fwd. end-to-end p50 latency improved ~12% on that run.
maria: nice. still want to instrument to catch regressions: add nsys sampling on dedicated regression job and baseline before merging. can ci-bot schedule?
ci-bot: scheduled perf job: nvprof+nsys baseline run queued on perf-cluster (job 4150001290). will post artifacts to /perf/traces/4150001290 once done. :white_check_mark:
jon: next steps: 1) write unit test for eviction coalescing correctness 2) add heuristic flag so we can toggle prefetch_window in prod 3) CI perf job with nsys sampling & perfetto diff 4) monitor kernel top-10 by time in dashboards
ale x: I'll open a PR with coalesced kernel + feature flag. tagging @maria @leena for review. PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4234
maria: ping on the PR when ready. also add nvprof snippet to the PR description so reviewers can see before/after numbers quickly.
leena: let's also add a quick eval that runs with seq=512 and seq=1024 since the eviction dynamics shift with sequence length.
alex: will do. thanks all. :raised_hands:
